question: How do RRFBs normally operate with respect to activation, synchronization, and flash rate?
model_answer: Direct Answer: RRFBs must remain dark until actuated by a pedestrian, then flash for a predetermined period (or, with passive detection, until the pedestrian clears the crosswalk). All RRFB units serving a given crosswalk must start and stop flashing simultaneously. When flashing, each unit's two yellow indications must use a rapid flash rate of 75 flashing sequences per minute — a specific exception to the normal beacon flash rate. Standards (mandatory): - "The RRFB shall be normally dark, shall initiate operation only upon pedestrian actuation, and shall cease operation at a predetermined time after the pedestrian actuation or, with passive detection, after the pedestrian clears the crosswalk." - "All RRFB units associated with a given crosswalk (including those with an advance crossing sign, if used) shall, when activated, simultaneously commence operation of their rapid flashing indications and shall cease operation simultaneously." - "When activated, the two yellow indications in each RRFB unit shall flash in a rapidly flashing sequence. As a specific exception to the requirements for the flash rate of beacons provided in Paragraph 3 of Section 4S.01, RRFBs shall use a much faster flash rate and shall provide 75 flashing sequences per minute." Guidance (recommended): - "The minimum duration of a predetermined period of operation of the RRFBs following each actuation should be based on the procedures for the timing of pedestrian clearance times for pedestrian signals (see Section 4I.06)." Options (permitted): - "A pedestrian-activated and/or bicyclist-activated rectangular rapid flashing beacon (RRFB) may be used to provide supplemental emphasis to pedestrian, school, and trail warning signs at marked crosswalks across uncontrolled approaches." - "If used at intersections with two crosswalks on an uncontrolled approach, post-mounted RRFBs may be installed to face only one direction of travel at the first crosswalk that traffic encounters (see Figure 4L-1)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 4L-1 shows an example RRFB installation at uncontrolled, marked crosswalks at an intersection, with Note 1 stating that when activated, the RRFBs on both approaches shall simultaneously commence and cease operation of their rapid flashing indications. - [Image 2] The full page view of the Section 4L.03 Standard text shows the normally-dark/actuation-only requirement, the simultaneous start-and-stop requirement, the 75-flashing-sequences-per-minute rate, and the detailed 800-millisecond left/right flashing sequence (steps A–G). - [Image 3] The continuation page shows the remainder of the flashing sequence (steps H–L) and the Standard that the flash rate of each individual RRFB indication shall not be more than 5 flashes per second, to avoid frequencies that might cause seizures. - [Image 4] The full page view containing Figure 4L-1 reiterates in the figure notes that RRFBs on both approaches shall simultaneously commence and cease operation. - [Image 5] The full page view of Sections 4L.01–4L.02 shows the Option that a pedestrian- and/or bicyclist-activated RRFB may be used at marked crosswalks across uncontrolled approaches. Citations: - Section 4L.03 Standard §1 (p.738) - Section 4L.03 Standard §2 (p.738) - Section 4L.03 Standard §6 (p.738) - Section 4L.03 Guidance §3 (p.738) - Section 4L.01 Option §1 (p.736) - Section 4L.02 Option §11 (p.738) - Figure 4L-1 (p.737) - Page 779 - Page 780 - Page 778 - Page 777
gold_answer: They are normally dark and operate only upon pedestrian actuation, stopping after the predetermined period or after a detected pedestrian clears. All RRFB units for the crosswalk begin and end together. When active, they use 75 rapid-flashing sequences per minute.
